f.title: Submit clinical trial safety reports and ICSRs via the MCAZ e-PV portal
f.statement: Clinical trial safety reports or individual case safety reports (AEs, ADRs, SAEs and AEFIs) are submitted via the MCAZ online e-PV portal.

rows.quote:
There is also provision for submission
of clinical trial safety reports or individual case safety reports (ICSRs) (AEs, ADRs,
SAEs & AEFIs) via the online portal found at https://e-pv.mcaz.co.zw/
rows.review_note: Review: descriptive ('there is provision'); recorded as Permitted channel; the mandatory use of e-PV is captured in the 5.21.2 row. Double-check: 85.

f.title: Investigator must ensure all SAEs are reported promptly to MCAZ, sponsor and ethics committee
f.statement: The investigator should ensure that all serious adverse events are reported promptly to the MCAZ, the sponsor and the Ethics Committee, and that proper protection procedures or treatments are administered to participants with serious adverse events.

rows.quote:
5.6.4.8 The investigator should ensure that all serious adverse events are reported
promptly to the MCAZ, sponsor and the Ethics Committee. Proper
protection procedures or treatments should be administered to trial
participants with serious adverse events.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended (the timed, mandatory duty is in 5.21.2). Double-check: OK.

f.title: Provide medical care to participants for trial-related adverse events
f.statement: During and following a participant's participation in a trial, the investigator should ensure adequate medical care is provided for any adverse events, including clinically significant laboratory values, related to the trial.

rows.quote:
During and following a participant’s participation in a trial, the investigator
should ensure adequate medical care is provided to a participant for any
adverse events including clinically significant laboratory values related to the
trial.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Location heading inferred from the section order (5.6). Double-check: 88.

f.title: Report all AEs to MCAZ and expedite SAEs to the ethics committee and MCAZ
f.statement: The sponsor should report to the MCAZ all adverse events occurring during the trial and should expedite reporting of all serious adverse events to the Ethics Committee and the MCAZ; the sponsor and investigators should immediately undertake appropriate measures and treatment to protect trial participants.
f.exceptions: Per 5.21.2, non-serious AEs are not submitted routinely but as line listings with annual reports.

rows.quote:
5.7.2.15 The sponsor should report to the MCAZ, all adverse events occurring during the
course of the trial. The sponsor should expedite reporting all serious adverse
events to the Ethics Committee and the MCAZ and the sponsor and the
investigators should immediately undertake appropriate and necessary
measures and treatment to protect the trial participants.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Conflicts in part with 5.21.2 (non-serious AEs only in annual line listings); exception recorded. Double-check: internal inconsistency; 85.

f.title: Provide an up-to-date investigator brochure
f.statement: The sponsor should provide an up-to-date Investigator's Brochure including the products' physical, chemical, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties from animals and humans and currently available results of relevant clinical trials.

rows.quote:
5.7.2.5 The sponsor should provide an up to date Investigator’s brochure, which includes
information about the products with respect to their physical,
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: 88.

f.title: Ensure sufficient safety data support the proposed human exposure
f.statement: The sponsor should ensure that sufficient safety and efficacy data from non-clinical studies and/or clinical trials are available to support human exposure by the route, dosages, duration and trial population to be studied.

rows.quote:
5.7.2.6 The sponsor should ensure that sufficient safety and efficacy data from non-
clinical studies and/or clinical trials are available to support human exposure by
the route, at the dosages for the duration and in the trial population to be studied.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: 88.

f.title: Blinding codes must allow rapid identification in a medical emergency
f.statement: In blinded trials, the coding system for investigational products should include a mechanism that permits rapid identification of the products in case of a medical emergency but does not permit undetectable breaks of the blinding.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Safety system configuration

rows.quote:
5.7.2.9 In blinded trials, the coding system for the IP’s should include a mechanism that
permits rapid identification of the products in case of a medical emergency but
does not permit undetectable breaks of the blinding.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Inform the ethics committee and MCAZ of premature termination or suspension and reasons
f.statement: When a trial is prematurely terminated or suspended by the sponsor or investigators, the Ethics Committee and MCAZ/institution should be informed of the decision and the reasons; whether completed or prematurely terminated, the sponsor should submit a report to the MCAZ and institution within 30 days.

rows.deadline: Report within 30 days of completion or premature termination
rows.quote:
5.7.2.16 When a trial is prematurely terminated or suspended by the sponsor/investigators,
the Ethics Committee and MCAZ/institution should be informed of the
decision to terminate/suspend the trial and the reasons thereof by the
sponsor/investigators.
5.7.2.17 Whether the trial is completed or prematurely terminated, the sponsor should
submit a report to the MCAZ and institution within 30 (thirty) days.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. No deadline_rule: the clock start (completion or termination date) is implied, not worded. Kept for the safety relevance of termination. Double-check: 85.

f.title: Retain trial documents and participant identification codes for at least 10 years
f.statement: The protocol, documents, case report forms, informed consent forms and other trial-related documents should be retained for at least 10 years by the sponsor, participant documents for at least 10 years by the medical institution, and participant identification codes for at least 10 years by the investigator and the sponsor.
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.quote:
5.8.4 The protocol, documents, case report forms, Informed Consent Forms and other
trial- related documents should be retained for at least 10 years by the sponsor;
and the trial participants documents should be retained for at least 10 years by
the medical institution. The participant identification codes should be retained by
the investigator and the sponsor for at least 10 years.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit requested records within 48 hours if safety concerns arise
f.statement: The sponsor must keep all records related to the conduct of a clinical trial in a format that facilitates verification for inspection, and must submit requested records within 48 hours if safety concerns arise.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Clinical safety monitoring

rows.deadline: Within 48 hours of the request where safety concerns arise
rows.quote:
5.8.6 The sponsor must keep all records related to the conduct of a clinical trial in a
format that facilitates verification for the purpose of an inspection.
5.8.7 The sponsor must submit requested records within 48 hours if safety concerns
arise.
rows.review_note: Review: must = Mandatory. Clock start is the request; clock_start quotes 'submit requested records' as the nearest wording. Double-check: clock wording approximate; 85.

deadline_rule.applies_to: Records requested by MCAZ where safety concerns arise

f.title: Maintain records of all local and international adverse events of the drug and IB changes
f.statement: The sponsor must maintain complete and accurate records of the use of a drug in a clinical trial, including all versions of the investigator's brochure, records of each change with rationale and supporting documentation, records of all adverse events of the drug occurring locally or internationally (with indication and dosage form at the time), and enrolment records enabling all participants to be identified and contacted if the drug may endanger their health.
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Data integrity & records

rows.quote:
5.8.9 The sponsor must maintain complete and accurate records in respect of the use
of a drug in a clinical trial, including:
i. A copy of all versions of the investigator's brochure for the drug;
ii. Records respecting each change made to the investigator's brochure,
including the rationale for each change and documentation that
supports each change;
iii. Records for all adverse events in respect of the drug that have occurred
locally or internationally, including information that specifies the
indication for use and the dosage form of the drug at the time of the
adverse
event;
rows.review_note: Review: must = Mandatory; item iv (enrolment records for contact) cited in the statement from the next item. Double-check: 88.

f.title: Protocol must describe safety assessment and AE reporting procedures
f.statement: The protocol should describe the assessment of safety, including procedures for eliciting reports of and for recording and reporting adverse events and intercurrent illnesses, and the type and duration of follow-up of participants after adverse events.
f.clause: 5.13.1.8 Clinical trial protocol - Assessment of safety

rows.quote:
iii. Procedures for eliciting reports of and for recording and reporting adverse
event and Inter-current illnesses.
iv. The type and duration of the follow-up o participants after adverse events
rows.location: 5.13.1.8 Clinical trial protocol - Assessment of safety
rows.review_note: Review: the source's items i-ii under 'Assessment of Safety' repeat the efficacy wording (apparent drafting error), so only iii-iv are curated. Modal implicit; Recommended. Double-check: 82.

f.title: Sponsor may establish an IDMC with written procedures and meeting records
f.statement: The sponsor may consider establishing an independent data-monitoring committee to assess at intervals the progress of the trial, including the safety data and critical efficacy endpoints, and to recommend whether to continue, modify or stop the trial; the IDMC should have written operating procedures and maintain written records of all its meetings.

rows.quote:
ii. The sponsor may consider establishing an independent data-monitoring
committee (IDMC) to assess the progress of a clinical trial, including
the safety data and the critical efficacy endpoints at intervals, and to
recommend to the sponsor whether to continue, modify, or stop a trial.
The IDMC should have written operating procedures and maintain
written records of all its meetings.
rows.review_note: Review: may = Permitted (establishment); should for procedures and records once established. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Notify investigators and authorities when clinical development of the product is discontinued
f.statement: If the sponsor discontinues the clinical development of an investigational product, it should maintain sponsor-specific essential documents for at least ten years after formal discontinuation and notify all trial investigators/institutions and all the regulatory authorities.

rows.quote:
viii. If the sponsor discontinues the clinical development of an
investigational product, the sponsor should notify all the trial
investigators/institutions and all the regulatory authorities.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended; retention element (vii) mentioned in statement. Double-check: 86.

f.title: Investigator must promptly report SUSARs and new safety information to the IRB/IEC and MCAZ
f.statement: The investigator should promptly report to the IRB/IEC and MCAZ: deviations or changes to eliminate immediate hazards to subjects; changes increasing risk to subjects; all adverse drug reactions that are both serious and unexpected; and new information that may adversely affect the safety of subjects or the conduct of the trial.
f.topic: SUSAR and new safety information reporting

rows.quote:
5.16.2 The investigator should promptly report to the IRB/IEC and MCAZ:
i. Deviations from, or changes of, the protocol to eliminate immediate
hazards to the trial subjects
ii. Changes increasing the risk to subjects and/or affecting significantly the
conduct of the trial
iii. 5.16.2.3All adverse drug reactions (ADRs) that are both serious and
unexpected.
iv. New information that may affect adversely the safety of the subjects or the
conduct of the trial.
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit all AEs, ADRs, SAEs and AEFIs to MCAZ via the e-PV system, with logs and DSMB reports
f.statement: It is a mandatory requirement that all adverse event reports (AEs, ADRs, SAEs and AEFIs, known and unknown) are submitted to MCAZ via the online e-PV system; if the system cannot be accessed, hard copies including causality outcome by the sponsor and participant management should be submitted. Safety report summaries (AE/SAE/AEFI logs) and DSMB/DMC interim data analysis reports are required.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
f.exceptions: Non-serious AEs and foreign ICSRs are not submitted routinely (see separate rows).

rows.quote:
It is a mandatory requirement that all AEs reports (AEs, ADRs, SAEs and
AEFIs known and unknown must be submitted to the MCAZ via the online e-
PV system found on https://e-pv.mcaz.co.zw/ In the event that there are any
challenges accessing the online e-PV system hard copies of the safety should be
submitted to MCAZ including causality outcome by the sponsor and participant
management. The safety report summaries including known & unknown as AE/
SAE/AEFI log and DSMB/DMC interim data analysis reports are required.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: 'mandatory requirement ... must' = Mandatory. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Report SAEs to MCAZ no later than 7 calendar days after the investigator knows of them
f.statement: Serious adverse events during the trial must be reported promptly to the MCAZ as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days after the occurrence becomes known to the principal investigator(s); the SAE report form should be complete and detailed, including information such as laboratory results to enable causality assessment.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
f.applicability: SAEs in clinical trials in Zimbabwe

rows.deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 7 calendar days of occurrence being known by the principal investigator
rows.quote:
Reports of serious adverse events (SAEs) during the trial must be reported
promptly to the MCAZ as soon as possible but no later than 7 calendar days of
occurrence being known by the principal investigator/investigators. The serious
adverse events (SAE) report form should be completed and detailed, information
such as laboratory results submitted to enable causality assessment of the report.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: must = Mandatory; replaces the earlier 48-hour limit (per the change history in the document). Double-check: OK.

deadline_rule.clock_start:
of
occurrence being known by the principal investigator/investigators
deadline_rule.applies_to: Serious adverse events during the trial

f.title: Submit SAE follow-up information within 8 additional calendar days
f.statement: Follow-up information on SAEs should be submitted as soon as it becomes available within 8 additional calendar days; it should be clearly marked as update information and include the protocol number and volunteer ID number.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.deadline: Within 8 additional calendar days (after the initial SAE report)
rows.quote:
Follow-up information should also be submitted as soon as it becomes available
within 8 additional calendar days.. Additional information may include copies
of diagnostic test results, laboratory reports, or medical record progress notes.
All additional information should be clearly marked as update information and
should include the Protocol Number and Volunteer ID Number.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. The clock runs from the initial 7-day report ('additional'); clock_start quotes that wording. Double-check: clock start relative; 84.

f.title: The principal investigator is responsible for reporting safety reports to MCAZ
f.statement: The principal investigator is responsible for reporting safety reports to the Authority.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting

rows.quote:
The principal investigator is responsible for reporting safety reports to the
Authority.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: 'is responsible' = Mandatory. Sponsor role in the same section (causality, hard copies) noted elsewhere. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit non-serious AEs only as line listings and summaries with annual reports
f.statement: Non-serious adverse events should not be submitted to MCAZ routinely but should be submitted as line listings and summaries with the annual reports; the Authority may request further information.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting

rows.quote:
Non-serious adverse events should not be submitted to MCAZ on a routine basis
but should be submitted as line listings and summaries during the submission of
annual reports.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. Double-check: OK.

f.title: Report foreign ICSRs within 7 days only for major safety issues or on request
f.statement: Foreign individual case safety reports should not be submitted routinely but should be reported within 7 days when there is a major safety issue or regulatory decision which impacts or changes the risk-benefit profile of the product, or on specific request by the Authority.
f.clause: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
f.processes: Submission operations; Clinical safety monitoring; Regulatory intelligence

rows.deadline: Within 7 days (major safety issue or regulatory decision, or on request)
rows.quote:
Foreign individual case safety reports should not be submitted to the Authority on
a routine basis but should be reported within 7 days when there is a major safety
issue or regulatory decision which impacts/changes the risk-benefit profile of the
product or on specific request by the Authority.
rows.location: 5.21.2 Monitoring of clinical trials including safety reporting
rows.review_note: Review: should = Recommended. The 7 days have no explicit start; clock_start quotes the triggering condition. Days read as calendar days. Double-check: clock ambiguous; 82.

when there is a major safety

f.title: Observe all authorisation conditions imposed for participant safety
f.statement: For the safety of all persons taking part in the trial, the person conducting the trial shall observe strictly all the conditions subject to which the trial is authorised.
f.clause: 5.21.4 Conditions for conduct of clinical trials

rows.actor: Person conducting the trial (sponsor / principal investigator)
rows.quote:
for the safety of all persons or
animals taking part in such trial, the person conducting the trial shall observe
strictly all the conditions participant to which the trial is authorized.
rows.location: 5.21.4 Conditions for conduct of clinical trials
rows.review_note: Review: shall = Mandatory (restates MASCA). Double-check: OK.

f.title: Submit a comprehensive report on serious adverse effects within 90 days of trial completion
f.statement: Not later than 30 days after completion of a clinical trial, the person who conducted it shall submit a preliminary report on the ethical evaluation of the trial, and not later than 90 days after completion a comprehensive report on any serious or adverse effects or reactions established by the trial.
f.clause: 5.21.5 Annual progress reports, preliminary, final reports and publications

rows.actor: Person who conducted the trial (principal investigator)
rows.deadline: Not later than 90 days after completion of the trial
rows.quote:
In addition to the report
referred to above, the person who conducted the trial shall, not later than 90
days after the completion of the trial, compile and submit to the Secretary
through the Authority (MCAZ) a comprehensive report or any serious or
adverse effects or reaction established by the trial.
rows.location: 5.21.5 Annual progress reports, preliminary, final reports and publications
rows.review_note: Review: shall = Mandatory (quoted from MASCA). The 30-day preliminary ethics report is mentioned in the statement but is not a safety report and has no row. Double-check: OK.

deadline_rule.clock_start: after the completion of the trial
